html:
A revolt of the Messenians against Sparta, decades after their defeat in the First Messenian War. Dates vary in the sources; the chart follows one ancient reckoning of about 685 to 668 BCE, while many historians put it nearer 660 to 650 BCE.

The Messenians had help from Argos and Arcadia, and later legend made a hero of their leader Aristomenes. The war went badly for Sparta at first. The poet Tyrtaeus wrote marching songs urging Spartans to stand firm in the line, some of the earliest poems about hoplite warfare. In the end the revolt failed, and the Messenians became helots once more.

Many historians think the scare changed Sparta. To hold down a huge unfree population, it turned itself into a military society, with the strict training, common messes and laws later credited to Lycurgus and the Great Rhetra.
